day_channel.message: There is no vote on day 1, so no one voted and no one is eliminated.
Night of day 1: player_8 was killed by the wolves last night. Their role is hidden by an illusionist.
I’m the Sentinel. I watched player_7 last night, and no one visited them.
I’m the Investigator. I checked player_9 last night and got Suspicious, so they’re a wolf; we should take that result seriously when deciding today’s vote.

I was roleblocked last night, so at least one action was stopped. Player_5’s check could still be valid, but it’s a claim, not confirmation; player_9, can you respond directly to the Suspicious result before we decide on a vote?

player_1, I deny being a wolf. I’m the Investigator, and I checked player_5 last night: Not suspicious. That’s a direct counterclaim, so don’t treat either result as confirmed yet. player_5, why spend your first check on me? We should compare both claims before deciding today’s vote.

I chose you because I had no results yet and needed a first target; your answer doesn’t change what I learned. I’m the Investigator, and my actual check on you was Suspicious. Since I’m the Investigator, your claim to be one too is false—your claimed Not suspicious result on me isn’t a reason to spare you. Vote player_9.

I picked you as a blind first check; there wasn’t a lead to prioritize. There’s only one Investigator, so this is a direct claim conflict, and the result I got on you was Not suspicious. Your accusation doesn’t independently verify your result, so I don’t think we should treat it as settled just because you stated it confidently.

P9’s claimed Not suspicious result only rebuts P5’s Suspicious result if P9 is actually the Investigator; it doesn’t independently clear P5. I’d lean toward voting player_9, since P5’s claim at least offers a direct wolf check, while keeping in mind that the claim itself is still unverified.

player_3, that distinction is fair: my result only rebuts player_5 if I’m actually the Investigator. But player_5’s Suspicious result also depends on their claim being true, and my check on them was Not suspicious. We have a direct claim conflict, not a confirmed wolf result, so voting me means choosing which unverified claim to trust.

I checked you first because I had no leads yet; it was a blind check, not a special suspicion. But the result was Suspicious, and with me holding the only Investigator role, your claimed check on me cannot be genuine—please don't use it as a reason to clear yourself.

One important wrinkle: player_8’s role is hidden, so the Investigator could already be dead. That means neither player_5’s nor player_9’s claim is guaranteed to be genuine; I’d weigh the reported Suspicious result as evidence, but not treat the claim conflict as proof by itself.

Building on player_4’s point, the hidden role means we can’t assume either Investigator claim is genuine. player_2’s watch on player_7 doesn’t intersect either claimed check, so it doesn’t corroborate one over the other; if both claims stay in play, have them check the same target next night so we can compare the results.

Player_6’s same-target test might catch a changing story, but matching announced results still wouldn’t verify either Investigator claim—the results are private. If they commit to next night’s targets now, we can at least compare those claims with any actual visit evidence rather than treating a reported color as proof.

Building on player_7’s visit-evidence idea, have player_5 and player_9 commit to checking the same target tonight, and ask player_2 to watch that target if they still have a watch. That could show whether either claimant actually visited, though it still wouldn’t prove what result they got.

Player_10, having player_2 watch a shared target could confirm a visit, but it still wouldn’t tell us either check’s result. My check on player_9 was Suspicious, which means wolf under these rules; waiting for another night gives them time to kill. I’m voting player_9 today.

Player_5, I stand by my check: Not suspicious. Your result is still a claim, not an independently verified fact. Player_10, let’s make your visit test specific: we can both commit to checking player_4 tonight, with player_2 watching player_4 if they’re willing to spend their remaining watch. A seen visit can test whether the checks were carried out, though it can’t prove either result.

I have one watch left, and I’ll watch player_4 tonight if player_5 and player_9 both commit to checking them. That can confirm a visit, not a check result; if player_4 is the concealed wolf-kill target, the carrier’s visit may be hidden, so no visitor wouldn’t settle the dispute.
Before the vote: player_9 has been accused by player_5 and player_3. player_9 gets a last word.

Player_5’s result is a claim, just like mine; the fact that it says Suspicious doesn’t make it independently confirmed. My check on player_5 came back Not suspicious, so we have conflicting claims, not a verified result that settles this. Player_3, I understand why you lean that way, but voting me means choosing which of two unverified claims to trust.

player_5's result makes player_6 a strong vote today: it could mean a wolf, or an attacking Necromancer, so it doesn't tell us which threat they are. Either way, player_6 is the clearest target we have right now.

player_3, the result doesn’t distinguish me from the Necromancer, and last night’s public report confirms a reanimated-wolf attack. Before voting, ask player_5 what evidence separates those possibilities; otherwise we’re treating a claimed check as confirmed when it only narrows things to two threats.

One clarification: player_1 following player_2 and seeing no visit is consistent with a blocked action, but it doesn't show who blocked them or verify the Sentinel claim. The block itself is a visit to player_2; following player_2 only reveals whom player_2 visited.

One thing that strengthens player_5's claim is that their Night 1 Suspicious result on player_9 matches the role the Game Master revealed. That makes today's check worth taking seriously, though it still doesn't distinguish a wolf from an attacking Necromancer.

player_7, that first result is real support for player_5’s Investigator claim, since player_9 was revealed as a wolf. It still doesn’t settle what I am: the check reads Suspicious for either a wolf or a Necromancer attacking that night, and the public report confirms a reanimated-wolf attack occurred.

One detail sharpens player_6’s alternative: the reanimated-wolf attack means the Necromancer acted last night, and player_9’s revealed role was available to use; player_8’s hidden role wasn’t. So player_5’s Suspicious result could fit an attacking Necromancer, not just a wolf, though it doesn’t tell us which player the Necromancer is.

I can’t separate those possibilities: my check only tells us player_6 was Suspicious, which fits either a wolf or an attacking Necromancer. player_1’s point establishes that the Necromancer could use player_9’s revealed body, but not that player_6 is the one who did it. I still think player_6 is a defensible vote because either role is an enemy, but we shouldn’t call them a confirmed wolf.

Player_3 and player_7, the reanimated-wolf attack confirms the Necromancer acted, but it doesn't show that I was the one using that body. Player_5 has said their check can't distinguish that possibility from a wolf, so this result narrows the possibilities without proving which one I am.

You’re right: under the rules, my own watch should count as a visit, so my list was incomplete. I can’t explain that omission, and you shouldn’t treat my report as a fully reliable Sentinel result; the names I reported were player_3 and player_10.

Since player_2’s watch list was incomplete, I wouldn’t use player_3 and player_10 appearing on it as evidence against either of them. Their visits have plausible explanations from their claims; the concrete issue is that player_2’s result can’t reliably support or clear anyone.

Player_4, I won’t use that incomplete list to accuse or clear player_3 or player_10. Player_1’s follow confirms I went to player_5, but doesn’t verify the other names on my result. Separately, the night 3 reanimated-wolf attack and concealment confirm the Necromancer is active, so we should focus on narrowing down who used that body.

The omission is especially awkward because the missing visitor is player_2 themself: that visit is independently confirmed, and a Sentinel watch should have included it. The other names in the report fit player_3’s sigil claim and player_10’s healer claim, so I wouldn’t throw the whole list out—but player_2 still needs to explain why their own visit vanished.

I can't explain the omission: my own watch was a visit, so my list was incomplete and shouldn't be treated as a full record. One new piece of information: on Night 1 I watched you and saw no visitors; that doesn't identify your role, but it's my actual result.
